Re: Medical Necessity Appeal — Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease (PAD) Revascularization

Dear Medical Director / Utilization Review Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of authorization for lower extremity revascularization for my patient, who has been diagnosed with [Clinical Subset]. This procedure is medically necessary and is supported by the highest level of evidence from current societal guidelines.

CLINICAL SUMMARY

My patient presents with [Clinical Subset], requiring elective revascularization. Following comprehensive clinical evaluation, the recommended intervention is: [Primary recommendation text]



GUIDELINE SUPPORT

This recommendation is based on the 2024 ACC/AHA/AACVPR/APMA/ABC/SCAI/SVM/SVN/SVS/SIR/VESS Guideline for the Management of Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease (Gornik HL et al., Circulation. 2024;149(24):e1313–e410. PMID 38743805), which is the most current and comprehensive multisociety guideline on this topic.

The procedure (CPT: {{cpt_codes}}, ICD-10: {{icd_codes}}) is indicated for this patient based on the following evidence:

1. 2024 ACC/AHA PAD Guideline (Gornik HL et al., Circulation 2024, PMID 38743805): Class I/IIa recommendation for revascularization in patients with [Clinical Subset] when anatomically feasible and clinically appropriate.

2. BEST-CLI Trial (Menard MT et al., NEJM 2022): Demonstrated that revascularization significantly improves limb salvage and quality of life in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI).

3. BASIL-2 Trial (Bradbury AW et al., Lancet 2023): Confirmed the benefit of revascularization-first strategies in CLTI patients requiring below-the-knee intervention.

4. WIfI Classification (Mills JL et al., J Vasc Surg 2014): Validated risk stratification confirming that patients with higher WIfI stages derive the greatest benefit from revascularization.

MEDICAL NECESSITY

Without timely revascularization, this patient faces significant risk of:
• Major limb amputation
• Irreversible ischemic tissue loss
• Functional decline and loss of ambulation
• Markedly reduced quality of life

Conservative measures including guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) and supervised exercise therapy have been considered and/or attempted as appropriate. The patient's clinical presentation necessitates revascularization as the next appropriate step in care.

REQUESTED ACTION

I respectfully request that you overturn the denial and authorize the requested revascularization procedure. I am available to discuss this case further and can provide additional clinical documentation upon request.
